newsitem.title: USA: Intel sets $820 mln profit-sharing plan.
newsitem.headline: Intel sets $820 mln profit-sharing plan.

text.p: Intel Corp, the world's largest maker of semiconductor chips, on Tuesday said it would give its employees $820 million in cash bonuses and profit sharing for their record-breaking performance in 1996.
Craig Barrett, Intel's chief operating officer, said all employees would become eligible for stock options beginning in the company's next program to be launched in April.

"This outstanding year would not have been possible without the remarkable efforts of Intel employees around the world," said Barrett, who is slated to become president of Intel this spring, making him heir apparent to CEO Andy Grove.

Barrett said the company last year paid out $214 million, or the equivalent of 26.9 days' salary for each Intel employee, under the Employee Cash Bonus Program. All employees receive the cash profit-sharing in six-month installments.

In 1996, the company also extended its Employee Bonus profitability-based program to all employees. The plan, based on growth in Intel earnings and achievement of an employee's business group goals, paid out a total of $360 million.
A previously announced one-time bonus marking Intel's record-breaking year paid $1,000 to each U.S. employee and a locally adjusted figure to each non-U.S. employee, or a total of $45 million.

Intel said that for the ninth consecutive year it contributed the maximum allowed by law to its employee retirement program, or 12.5 percent of employees' pay -- a figure which totaled about $200 million.
